sam_support: Customer ACME hitting 402 on POST /v1/generate, says console shows \"billing error\" and there is no request id in the UI. Customer on mobile (Android) and a proxy in front of our API. Can we get a tight repro ask to send them?

maria_engineer: Quick checklist to request from them (keep it minimal):
- curl that reproduces the 402 (mask secrets)
- HAR from browser or curl (if they used web) or a curl copy from the app proxy
- SDK debug logs (enable debug flag) and a debug token if available
- Any proxy/nginx access log lines around the request time

maria_engineer: Example curl to ask for (they should replace token/ids):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -H \"x-rd-request-id: <if-you-see-it-in-network-tab>\" \
  --data-raw '{"input":"hello"}'
```

maria_engineer: If they have a HAR, ask them to export it and attach. If they only have a captured curl (Chrome -> Copy -> Copy as cURL), that works too.

josh_devex: Mobile-specific steps:
- Android: enable SDK debug: set `RD_SDK_DEBUG=true` (or call `Redwood.setDebug(true)`), reproduce, then run `adb logcat -T \"2026-03-17 00:00:00\" | grep -i redwood` and attach the lines.
- iOS: enable logging in SDK, reproduce, grab device console from Xcode (Devices -> Console) for the time window.

josh_devex: If they can’t turn on debug in prod, ask for nearest-second timestamps of the failing request + the app version + device time zone. We can then correlate in our logs.

lee_oncall: Proxy hint: many proxies strip unknown headers. Ask their infra to grep their proxy logs for the request time. Example for nginx access logs:
```
# on proxy host (example)
sudo zgrep "POST /v1/generate" /var/log/nginx/access*.gz | grep \"2026-03-17\" | sed -n '1,200p'
# look for x-rd-request-id or our User-Agent: RedwoodSDK
```

lee_oncall: Also ask them to search for our User-Agent or endpoints in the edge logs if they can't find a request id. Sometimes CDNs replace headers — a proxy capture is the fastest way to prove header loss.

maria_engineer: If they can generate one, ask them to create a debug token from Console -> Support -> Generate debug token (copy the token to us). If they can't use console, have them run the SDK debug flow and paste the `rd_debug_token` printed in logs (mask the rest).

support_bot: debug token created (masked): dt_************ (created by sam_support for acme@example.com) :white_check_mark:

maria_engineer: How to bundle for us (one ZIP):
- har.har (if available) OR curl.txt (copy-as-curl)
- sdk-logs.txt (log lines with timestamps)
- proxy-snippet.txt (3-5 nginx access lines around timestamp)
- debug-token.txt (if generated)
- brief.txt (one-line reproducible steps + device/timezone)

maria_engineer: Command to make a zip quickly: `zip -r acme-debug-3032104321.zip har.har sdk-logs.txt proxy-snippet.txt debug-token.txt brief.txt`

sam_support: I'll send this to the customer with a templated ask. Will request exact UTC timestamps for the failure window (±30s) and ask them to redact Authorization tokens before uploading.

josh_devex: If they send only a curl and we still don't see a request id, we can ask them to add a temporary header so we can match it through the proxy: `-H \"x-cust-correlation: acme-3032104321\"` and then search logs for that string.

sam_support: Perfect. Thanks all — sending now. :pray:
